subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw expose this egress firewall as a narrow web_fetch hostname policy, a cross-tool local fetch/search/browser policy, or a managed-proxy-owned policy boundary?
rationale: The requested config becomes an operator-trusted security boundary, and the open related PRs implement incompatible ownership models that automation should not choose.

options.title: Approve narrow web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Use the existing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96333 direction as an interim web_fetch-only contract, with denylist/search/browser/proxy follow-ups tracked separately.

options.title: Design shared local egress policy
options.body: Pause narrow PRs until maintainers define one local contract across fetch, search, browser, redirects, cache, providers, and plugins.

options.title: Make managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Accept that app-owned egress policy lives in proxy.enabled and external operator policy rather than new local domain firewall keys.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Use the existing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96333 direction as an interim web_fetch-only contract, with denylist/search/browser/proxy follow-ups tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history across guarded fetch, SSRF helpers, and web_fetch docs/runtime touched by the boundary choice.
